heroHeadline: German Economy Shows Turnaround Signs as Merz Pushes Faster Reforms, Sugar Tax Leak Sparks Backlash
heroSubtitle: Germany's Q2 GDP was revised up to +0.3% quarter-on-quarter and the Ifo business climate index climbed to a one-year high of 88.8 in August, the clearest signs yet of a turnaround after three years of stagnation — even as the government trimmed its full-year 2026 forecast to 0.5% on Middle East energy pressure. Chancellor Merz used an August 23 cabinet retreat at Neuhardenberg to press ministers to accelerate pro-growth reforms on taxes, pensions, deregulation, and digitalization. A leaked Finance Ministry draft proposing a sugar tax on a wide range of drinks — including oat milk and diet sodas — prompted Finance Minister Klingbeil to rule out taxing sugar-free beverages on August 26. Germany also deported 23 Afghan men to Kabul on August 25, bringing the total removed since Merz took office to roughly 228.
footerNote: Data sourced from official German federal records (Bundesarchiv, Bundestag, Bundesregierung), major German and international media, and EU/NATO/international bodies. Historical data draws on scholarly consensus.
